Objetivo

Construir dos repositorios nuevos, separados del monorepo actual:

1. `Vibe-Intelligence-Engine` — producto privado/prototipo de inteligencia de mercado, radar de Facebook, orquestación multi-modelo, análisis de oportunidades, generación de contenido y analytics.
2. `Vibe-Coding-Sin-Saber-Programar` — repositorio público educativo que enseña Vibe Coding estructurado, no prompt-first development, arquitectura, planificación, agentes, OpenCode y plantillas reutilizables.

> Nota: el conector actual de GitHub no expone creación de repositorios. Este issue sirve como especificación ejecutable para OpenCode y como registro público del plan. No crear los proyectos dentro de este monorepo salvo documentación puente.

## Prompt maestro para OpenCode

Actúa como arquitecto principal, ingeniero de software senior, DevOps, especialista en agentes LLM, seguridad y documentación técnica. No improvises y no reescribas estructuras sin justificarlo.

### Principios obligatorios

- No prompt-first development.
- Todo proyecto debe partir de problema, requisitos, alcance, arquitectura, modelo de datos, roadmap y tareas.
- La IA implementa tareas pequeñas y verificables, no aplicaciones completas con un prompt.
- Mantener documentación viva y sincronizada con el código.
- Usar `AGENTS.md` como contrato de trabajo para agentes y documentar equivalentes para otros ecosistemas cuando corresponda.
- Seguridad primero: jamás almacenar tokens, cookies, contraseñas, sesiones de Facebook, API keys ni datos personales reales.
- Facebook debe abordarse mediante acceso legítimo y revisión humana; no diseñar spam, evasión de controles, scraping agresivo ni publicación/comentario masivo.
- La automatización inicial debe centrarse en observación, clasificación, análisis, generación y aprobación humana.
- Cada decisión arquitectónica importante debe quedar documentada.

## REPO 1 — Vibe-Intelligence-Engine

Crear arquitectura preparada para evolucionar desde MVP local hacia SaaS.

### Objetivo funcional

Facebook/otras fuentes de señales → captura legítima → normalización → almacenamiento → clasificación semántica → detección de problema → intención → urgencia → oportunidad comercial → investigación → diagnóstico → generación de solución → generación multiformato de contenido → revisión humana → publicación controlada → métricas → aprendizaje.

### Componentes

- `apps/dashboard`
- `apps/content-studio`
- `services/facebook-radar`
- `services/analyzer`
- `services/opportunity-engine`
- `services/knowledge-engine`
- `services/content-engine`
- `services/analytics`
- `mcp/facebook-radar`
- `agents/`
- `database/`
- `docs/`
- `prompts/`
- `tests/`
- `.github/workflows/`

### Agentes iniciales

- orchestrator
- researcher
- facebook-analyst
- problem-classifier
- technical-diagnostician
- architect
- fact-checker
- content-strategist
- copywriter
- community-manager
- analytics
- monetization
- security-reviewer

### Flujo de análisis

Cada publicación candidata debe producir un registro estructurado con:

- fuente/grupo
- fecha
- texto normalizado
- enlace cuando sea legítimamente disponible
- tema
- herramienta/stack mencionado
- problema
- nivel estimado
- urgencia
- pain score
- helpability score
- content potential
- commercial potential
- intent score
- clasificación
- diagnóstico
- solución propuesta
- respuesta sugerida
- ideas de contenido
- estado de revisión humana
- resultado/engagement cuando exista

No guardar PII innecesaria. Preferir IDs/hash internos y metadatos mínimos.

### Orquestación multi-modelo

Diseñar una interfaz abstracta de proveedores/modelos para poder enrutar tareas diferentes a distintos modelos. No acoplar el producto a un único proveedor. Implementar primero un proveedor mock/local para pruebas y dejar adapters preparados.

El orchestrator debe poder encadenar:

`research → analyze → architect → fact-check → synthesize → content → review`

Cada agente debe tener entrada/salida estructurada y criterios de aceptación.

### Scoring inicial

Implementar un scoring explicable, configurable y testeable para:

- intent
- urgency
- pain
- helpability
- content potential
- commercial potential

No presentar scores como verdad objetiva; son señales internas.

### Content Engine

Una oportunidad puede generar:

- respuesta educativa para el grupo
- post de Facebook
- publicación LinkedIn
- carrusel
- guion de video corto
- artículo/tutorial
- guía GitHub
- CTA hacia el repositorio educativo

El contenido debe transformar la solución real, no copiar la publicación original. Debe evitar spam, claims inventados y engagement bait engañoso.

### Analytics

Medir, cuando los datos estén disponibles:

reach, impressions, reactions, comments, shares, clicks, GitHub visits, downloads, leads, conversions.

Crear feedback loop para descubrir qué problemas y formatos producen mejores resultados.

### MCP

Diseñar `facebook-radar` como MCP separado para que OpenCode pueda consultar/analizar oportunidades sin mezclar credenciales ni lógica de negocio. Diseñar adapters de navegador de forma desacoplada; cualquier integración Facebook debe cumplir las condiciones de acceso y políticas vigentes.

### Seguridad

- `.env.example`
- secret scanning
- gitleaks en CI
- datos reales fuera del repo
- logs sin tokens/cookies/PII
- threat model
- política de retención
- auditoría de acciones
- aprobación humana antes de cualquier acción externa

### Calidad

- TypeScript estricto si se usa TypeScript
- Python tipado si se usa Python
- lint
- format
- unit tests
- integration tests
- fixtures sintéticos
- CI
- Docker solo donde aporte valor
- README ejecutable
- ADRs

### Documentación

Crear:

- README.md
- AGENTS.md
- docs/vision.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/roadmap.md
- docs/model-orchestration.md
- docs/data-model.md
- docs/security.md
- docs/facebook-access.md
- docs/content-strategy.md
- docs/analytics.md
- docs/monetization.md
- docs/adr/
- docs/development/

Crear también GitHub Pages con MkDocs Material, manteniendo una estructura profesional y navegable.

## REPO 2 — Vibe-Coding-Sin-Saber-Programar

Debe ser público, educativo, práctico y completamente documentado.

### Mensaje central

“No necesitas saber programar para empezar a construir con IA. Pero sí necesitas aprender a dirigir un proyecto.”

### Metodología

`PROBLEM → SPECIFICATION → ARCHITECTURE → PLAN → TASK → IMPLEMENT → TEST → REVIEW → DOCUMENT → NEXT TASK`

### Estructura

- `01-fundamentos/`
- `02-antes-de-programar/`
- `03-arquitectura/`
- `04-planificacion/`
- `05-ia-y-agentes/`
- `06-opencode/`
- `07-git-y-github/`
- `08-pruebas-y-validacion/`
- `09-deploy-y-mantenimiento/`
- `10-proyectos/`
- `templates/`
- `examples/`
- `docs/`

### Plantillas obligatorias

- AGENTS.md
- PROJECT_SPEC.md
- REQUIREMENTS.md
- ARCHITECTURE.md
- DATABASE.md
- API.md
- ROADMAP.md
- TASKS.md
- ADR.md
- DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md
- SECURITY.md
- CHANGELOG.md

### Enseñar diferentes agentes

Explicar el patrón de instrucciones persistentes y adaptar ejemplos para OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code y Gemini sin vender una herramienta como única solución.

### Tutorial progresivo

El lector debe poder pasar de:

1. “No sé programar.”
2. entender qué es Vibe Coding.
3. definir un problema.
4. escribir requisitos.
5. diseñar arquitectura.
6. crear documentación para el agente.
7. instalar/configurar OpenCode.
8. pedir una primera tarea pequeña.
9. probarla.
10. revisar cambios.
11. continuar iterativamente.
12. desplegar.
13. mantener el proyecto.

### Proyectos educativos

Crear al menos ejemplos pequeños y completos, evitando proyectos gigantescos desde un único prompt. Cada ejemplo debe mostrar cómo se diseña antes de implementar.

### GitHub Pages

Crear `mkdocs.yml`, `docs/index.md` y navegación completa. El sitio debe ser público, claro para principiantes y útil también para desarrolladores.

## Site Pages

Replicar el estándar visual/documental que ya usa `Soluciona-Inteligencia-Artificial`: MkDocs Material, palette clara/oscura, búsqueda, navegación, `site_url`, `repo_url`, README + docs sincronizados y GitHub Actions para publicar Pages. No romper el formato existente. En cada nuevo repo, el README debe apuntar al sitio Pages y el sitio debe apuntar al repo.

## Orden de ejecución

1. Crear ambos repositorios si el entorno dispone de permiso/API para creación; si no, detener esa operación y documentar claramente la limitación.
2. Crear estructura base.
3. Crear AGENTS.md.
4. Crear documentación y ADRs.
5. Crear GitHub Pages.
6. Crear CI.
7. Implementar MVP del motor de datos y análisis con fixtures sintéticos.
8. Implementar interfaces de agentes y proveedor LLM mock.
9. Implementar Content Engine sin publicación automática.
10. Implementar dashboard mínimo.
11. Añadir tests.
12. Revisar seguridad.
13. Generar roadmap de siguientes iteraciones.

## Regla de trabajo para OpenCode

Antes de modificar código:

- leer `AGENTS.md`
- leer README
- leer arquitectura
- inspeccionar estructura real
- identificar tarea actual
- proponer cambios
- implementar la menor unidad funcional verificable
- ejecutar tests/lint/typecheck
- actualizar documentación
- registrar decisión relevante en ADR
- reportar exactamente qué se hizo, qué se verificó y qué queda pendiente.

No inventar APIs de Facebook. No asumir capacidades retiradas de Meta. No automatizar acciones que puedan convertirse en spam. No incluir credenciales reales.

Project Setup: ElysiaJS + Drizzle ORM + MySQL
## 1. Persiapan Proyek
- [ ] Inisialisasi proyek baru menggunakan `bun init` di root folder.
- [ ] Install dependensi utama: `elysia`, `drizzle-orm`, dan driver database MySQL (misalnya `mysql2` atau `postgres` tapi untuk mysql biasanya `mysql2`).
- [ ] Install dev-dependensi: `drizzle-kit` dan `@types/bun`.
- [ ] Setup file environment (`.env`) untuk menyimpan string koneksi database (`DATABASE_URL`).
## 2. Struktur Direktori
Buatkan struktur folder dasar berikut untuk memisahkan logika aplikasi:
```text
.
├── src/
│   ├── db/            # Konfigurasi koneksi database dan skema Drizzle
│   │   ├── schema.ts  # Definisi tabel-tabel database
│   │   └── index.ts   # Inisialisasi koneksi MySQL dan Drizzle
│   ├── routes/        # Definisi rute/endpoint API aplikasi
│   ├── controllers/   # Logika bisnis/handler untuk setiap endpoint
│   └── index.ts       # Entry point utama aplikasi Elysia
├── drizzle/           # File migrasi database (akan di-generate otomatis)
├── drizzle.config.ts  # File konfigurasi Drizzle Kit
├── .env               # File environment variables
├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json
```
## 3. Konfigurasi Database (Drizzle & MySQL)
- [ ] Buat file konfigurasi `drizzle.config.ts` untuk memberitahu Drizzle Kit di mana skema berada dan bagaimana cara koneksi ke database.
- [ ] Di `src/db/schema.ts`, definisikan skema tabel dasar (contoh: tabel `users`).
- [ ] Di `src/db/index.ts`, setup koneksi instance Drizzle ORM ke server MySQL.
## 4. Setup Server (ElysiaJS)
- [ ] Di `src/index.ts`, inisialisasi instance aplikasi ElysiaJS.
- [ ] Pasang (mount) rute-rute dari folder `src/routes/`.
- [ ] Jalankan server agar mendengarkan pada port tertentu (misalnya port 3000) dan pastikan ada log console yang menandakan server siap.
## 5. Skrip NPM & Migrasi
- [ ] Tambahkan skrip bantuan di `package.json` untuk mempermudah pengembangan:
  - `dev`: Menjalankan server menggunakan Bun dengan fitur hot-reload (`bun --watch src/index.ts`).
  - `db:generate`: Menjalankan Drizzle Kit untuk membuat file migrasi.
  - `db:migrate`: Menjalankan migrasi skema ke database MySQL.
- [ ] Lakukan percobaan generate dan migrasi pertama untuk memastikan koneksi ke MySQL berhasil.
- [ ] Lakukan pengujian ping/endpoint dasar untuk memastikan aplikasi Elysia berjalan sempurna.

[VIBE] 1500 — Bootstrap the branch's default bot as a Vibe project

**Priority:** P0 (foundation — every other issue in this reform depends on it)
**Kind:** feature (vibe bootstrap + cloud signup hook)
**Depends on:** nothing · **Blocks:** 1501, 1502, 1503, 1504

## Problem

Today a bot-kind Vibe project is only created when the user clicks "New Project".
The branch's **default bot** — the one created at branch creation (`create_cloud_workspace_inner`
at `botserver/crates/botcloud/src/integration.rs:600`, or by `drive_monitors.rs:566` when the
org comes from Drive) — exists only as a `bots` row + Drive files. People cannot "vibe" the
base bot: open Vibe and extend the bot they already talk to.

The reform (issues 1501/1502) moves bot sources to Forgejo. That requires **at least one
project bot per branch**: the default bot must exist as a Vibe project so it gets an ALM
org/repository and its sources move from Drive to git.

## Goal

When a branch is created (signup or "New Workspace"), a Vibe project named after the branch
is created automatically:

- `vibe_projects` row: `project_type = 'bot'`, `source_control = 'git'`, `branch_id` = the
  branch, `name` = branch slug (e.g. workspace `cristo` → project `cristo`).
- `bots` row association: the **existing** default bot row is bound to the project (id/uuid
  recorded in the project payload as `bot_id`), NOT duplicated — `ensure_vibe_bot_row`
  (`projects_api.rs:544`) must be taught to adopt the existing default bot instead of
  inserting a second row for the same slug.
- ALM provisioning (issue 1503): Forgejo org `{branch}` + repository `{branch}` are created
  and the default bot's Drive sources are imported as the initial commit (issue 1502 step 1).
- First-open experience: when the user opens General Bots and selects the default bot
  project in Vibe, they are vibing the base bot — chat with it, extend it, deploy it.

## Current behaviour (code anchors)

| What | Where |
|------|-------|
| Workspace/branch creation on signup | `botserver/crates/botcloud/src/api.rs:435` → `integration::create_cloud_workspace_inner` |
| Default bot created for org buckets without bots | `botserver/src/main_module/drive_monitors.rs:566` (`bot_names.insert(branch_slug)`) |
| Vibe project creation (idempotent, unique `(branch_id, name)`) | `botserver/crates/botvibe/src/projects.rs` `create()` |
| Bot-kind project → bots row (always INSERT, never adopts) | `botserver/crates/botvibe/src/projects_api.rs:544` `ensure_vibe_bot_row` |
| Bot project kind | `botserver/crates/botvibe/src/projects.rs:52` `ProjectKind::Bot` |

## Implementation plan

1. **`botserver/crates/botcloud/src/integration.rs`** — extend
   `create_cloud_workspace_inner(conn, branch_id, name)`: after creating the workspace row,
   call a new `botvibe::bootstrap::ensure_branch_default_project(branch_id, org_id, name)`
   (feature-gated `saas`/`vibe`; on cold start botvibe may not be linked — return early
   with a warn instead of failing signup).
2. **New `botserver/crates/botvibe/src/bootstrap.rs`**:
   - `ensure_branch_default_project(pool, org_id, branch_id, name) -> Result<Uuid, String>`
   - Idempotent: look up `vibe_projects WHERE branch_id = $1 AND name = $2` first
     (`ProjectRegistry::create` is already idempotent — reuse it).
   - Look up the default `bots` row for `(branch_id, slug = bot_slug(name))`; if found,
     write `payload.bot_id = bots.id` and `payload.bot_origin = 'drive'` (adopted), so
     chat/WS identity keeps working unchanged. Only insert a bots row when none exists.
   - Trigger git-mode provisioning lazily (issue 1503) on first Vibe open, NOT inline in
     signup (signup must stay fast; Forgejo down must not break onboarding).
3. **`ensure_vibe_bot_row`** (`projects_api.rs:544`): when `payload.bot_id` is present,
   verify the bot exists and return early (no INSERT). Keeps `origin='vibe'` semantics for
   non-bootstrap projects.
4. **Drive-created orgs** (`drive_monitors.rs` `ensure_cloud_workspace` path): call the same
   bootstrap after `ensure_branch_exists` so orgs born from Drive also get the project.
   Guard with `LoadOnly`/LOAD_ONLY respect — do not bootstrap when the flag is set.
5. **Migration/backfill** (one-shot, safe to re-run): SQL or a `botvibe` startup hook that
   scans `cloud_workspaces` and creates the missing default project per branch. Log a
   summary (`[vibe-bootstrap] branch X → project Y (bot adopted|created)`).
6. **UI**: `botui/ui/suite/vibe` project list must show the bootstrap project with kind
   `bot`; the Chat window already binds via `{ bot: slug }` for bot-kind projects
   (`vibe-shell/10_toolbar.js` `openChat`) — verify the adopted default bot slug matches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Signup (free/shared) creates workspace + branch + default bot + **Vibe project** in one flow.
- [ ] Opening Vibe shows the default bot project without any manual "New Project".
- [ ] Chat with the default bot via Vibe Chat button works (WS binds to the adopted bots row).
- [ ] Re-running bootstrap (server restart, repeated signup replay) creates nothing twice.
- [ ] A branch created only by `drive_monitor` (`.gborg` uploaded via `mc`) also gets the project.
- [ ] `bottest` integration test: signup → `vibe_projects` contains 1 bot-kind project for the branch.

## Non-goals

- Moving the bot's `start.bas` content itself (issue 1502).
- Test/prod twin bots (issue 1504).

Goal

Create a new Answer-page content cluster for people who **know the kind of RPG experience they want, but do not yet know which system fits it**.

The core search intent is not usually “give me a taxonomy of RPG systems”. It is closer to:

> “What RPG should I play if I want *this* vibe?”

Examples:

- What RPG should I play for an over-the-top space opera?
- What RPG feels like Borderlands / Guardians of the Galaxy?
- What RPG is good for a space western campaign?
- What RPG works well for political intrigue?
- What RPG should I use for gothic vampire drama?
- What RPG works for conspiracy / X-Files-style horror?
- What RPG is good for heist campaigns?
- What RPG should I play if I want rules-light fantasy exploration?

This should become a coherent discovery cluster rather than a pile of generic “top 10 RPGs” listicles.

## Why this fits Codex Cryptica

This intent is a natural acquisition bridge into CC:

```text
I want a certain campaign vibe
    ↓
Which systems support that experience?
    ↓
What does each system actually emphasise in play?
    ↓
Pick / investigate a system
    ↓
Build the setting, factions, NPCs, rumours, locations, heists, etc. in CC
```

CC already has system-neutral generators and themed `/for` content that can provide a useful next step after the user has chosen a game style.

It also complements the existing system-reference work (e.g. `systemsThatSupportThis`) and the existing Answer:

- `/answers/what-rpg-system-should-we-try-instead-of-dnd`

## Proposed cluster

Register a content cluster / intent along the lines of:

```text
rpg-system-selection
```

Intent definition:

> The user knows the genre, tone, play style, campaign structure or media inspiration they want and is looking for RPG systems that support that experience.

Pages may also belong to secondary clusters such as `space-opera`, `heists`, `solo-rpg`, `political-intrigue`, `vampire`, etc.

## Primary page type: vibe → system

Prioritise these.

Each Answer should:

- answer the vibe / campaign question directly near the top
- recommend a **small, genuinely differentiated set** of systems
- explain *why* each system fits using actual play style, mechanics, campaign structure or tone
- explain important differences between the options rather than simply listing games
- note where a system is a partial fit or needs adaptation
- link to authoritative publisher / SRD / official material where practical
- avoid implying official affiliation
- link onward to relevant CC tools and topic pages where useful

The page should help the reader understand trade-offs such as:

- cinematic vs tactical
- narrative vs crunchy
- episodic vs campaign-focused
- crew / faction play vs individual character focus
- lethal vs heroic
- rules-light vs rules-heavy
- sandbox vs mission-based

## Secondary page type: system → experience

Useful supporting pages may answer questions such as:

- What kind of game is Scum & Villainy?
- What does Mothership play like?
- Is Stars Without Number good for space opera?
- What sort of campaign is Blades in the Dark best suited to?

Do **not** create these automatically for every system. Add them only when there is real search/discovery value and enough original useful content.

## Initial candidate queries

Start with a small curated set, then expand from real demand:

### Sci-fi / space
- What RPG should I play for an over-the-top space opera?
- What RPG feels like Borderlands or Guardians of the Galaxy?
- What RPG should I use for a space western campaign?
- What RPG is good for gritty spaceship horror?
- What RPG is good for sandbox space exploration?

### Fantasy / adventure
- What RPG should I play for low-prep fantasy adventure?
- What RPG works for political intrigue and faction play?
- What RPG is good for heist campaigns?
- What RPG is good for exploration-focused sandbox play?

### Horror / modern
- What RPG should I play for gothic vampire drama?
- What RPG works for conspiracy / X-Files-style horror?
- What RPG is good for investigative cosmic horror?

### Play style
- What RPG is good for solo play?
- What RPG is good for one-shots?
- What RPG is good for long campaign play?
- What RPG is good for players who want rules-light roleplay?

## Content quality guardrails

Do **not** generate hundreds of pages from a Cartesian product of systems × genres × vibes.

Avoid thin SEO pages such as:

- “Best RPG for X” pages where the same paragraph is reused with swapped names
- pages that list systems without explaining actual play differences
- pages based only on broad genre labels when a stronger existing Answer already covers the intent

Prefer roughly 10–20 strong, evidence-backed pages initially and expand based on Search Console, analytics, Reddit/community questions and LLM visibility results.

## CC funnel / contextual CTA

After answering the system-selection question, link to genuinely relevant CC workflows rather than a generic product CTA.

Example for space opera:

- Star System Generator
- Faction / Faction Roster Generator
- Rumour Generator
- Personality / NPC tools
- relevant Space Opera `/for` or topic page

Example for political intrigue:

- Faction Generator
- Council Vote Generator
- Rumour Generator
- faction / intrigue Answers and examples

The Answer must remain useful if the reader never clicks a CC generator.

## Topic hub

Assess whether this cluster warrants a public topic hub after the first pages exist.

Possible routes / concepts:

- `/topics/rpg-systems`
- `/topics/find-an-rpg`
- `/topics/choose-an-rpg-system`

Do not create a thin directory. A hub should explain *how to choose a system for the experience you want* and then surface the strongest Answer pages.

## SEO / LLM discovery

These pages should explicitly connect:

```text
media / vibe inspiration
↔ genre
↔ play style
↔ mechanics / campaign structure
↔ RPG systems
↔ relevant CC tools
```

This is useful for both classic search and LLM retrieval because system-selection questions are often phrased relationally (“RPG like X”, “system for Y campaign”, “game with Z vibe”).

Requirements:

- concise direct answer near the top
- descriptive headings matching actual user questions
- strong internal links to related Answers, topic hubs and relevant generators
- appropriate content-cluster metadata / Intent Registry signals
- multiple-cluster membership where appropriate
- structured data using existing Answer conventions
- canonical, crawlable links to official system sources where practical
- avoid duplicate search intent with existing Answers

## Validation / discovery loop

Use real demand to decide what to publish next:

- Reddit / community questions
- Search Console queries
- Bing Webmaster / other search data where available
- CC internal searches / generator traffic
- LLM visibility benchmark questions

Where a specific community question inspires a page, capture the underlying intent rather than copying the wording verbatim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rpg-system-selection` (or equivalent) exists in the Intent Registry / content-cluster system
- [ ] Existing system-selection Answers are audited for overlap, especially `what-rpg-system-should-we-try-instead-of-dnd`
- [ ] Initial set of high-value vibe → system queries is prioritised
- [ ] Pages compare systems by actual play experience / mechanics, not just genre labels
- [ ] Relevant pages support multiple cluster memberships
- [ ] Each Answer links to appropriate CC tools/topics only where genuinely useful
- [ ] No programmatic thin-page explosion is introduced
- [ ] Search / analytics / LLM visibility can be measured for the cluster
- [ ] Topic hub is created only if there is enough material to make it genuinely useful

## Suggested first proof case

Use an **over-the-top / colourful space opera** Answer as the first implementation. This is based on a real community-style question seeking something in the vicinity of Borderlands / Guardians of the Galaxy rather than a named RPG system.
